title: OpenAI on Accidental Chain-of-Thought Grading
focus: understand why accidental chain-of-thought grading can distort AI evaluations and product claims
summary: AI HOT surfaced OpenAI's discussion of accidental chain-of-thought grading. This is important because evaluation design strongly affects what model benchmarks appear to prove, especially when reasoning traces leak into the scoring setup.
sourceNotes: A benchmark is only as trustworthy as the grading process behind it. If hidden reasoning or leaked answer structure helps the grader too much, the result may overstate real capability.
For builders and buyers, this is a reminder to treat model scores as signals rather than final truth, especially when benchmarks are used in launch marketing or tool comparisons.
cardSummary: Benchmark headlines deserve skepticism when evaluation design accidentally rewards leaked reasoning instead of genuine task performance.
readerLens: Benchmark stories matter most when they reveal how easy it is to overread scores from leaky evaluation setups.
watchlist: Which eval designs isolate answers from reasoning traces cleanly.
